title: I've now added a third shader option to my game(no moving lines).
author: Mekkablood
selftext:
Some weren't happy with the moving lines. I was going for a drawing 80's animation look but a lot of people don't like that apparently... and an option disabling the shaders(just using solid textures) also wasn't liked. Hopefully this offers a nice middle ground for everyone. Old shaders are still available.  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5541720/Gutter\_Scrap/?beta=0](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5541720/Gutter_Scrap/?beta=0)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Mekkablood please share some more about how you used AI in developing this. Naming the tools or saying "made with AI" doesn't count. Rule 4 is how we keep promotional posts contributing, by having them talk about the process and how the game was made. Trying to keep the sub focused on dev. This post may be removed if it isn't updated.

replies.author: Aligyon
replies.body: Huge improvement! It really makes the game stand out!

comments.author: ArchitectNebulous
comments.body: This one is much easier to focus on the game with.  Good work.

comments.author: Dangerous-Eye-215
comments.body: Nice job, that looks a lot better than the moving lines one I saw before.

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body:
No moving lines should be the default. Now it looks like a playable game.

Edit: another idea you can try is a post processing filter of the lines moving but not on the actual meshes. Think like a psx shader where everything is drawn over the game so it has a pixelated look. Just my two cents. Might not be feasible for what you want.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body:
The game itself looks interesting and fun to build a bot and fight, but its not my art style preference. Even after this fix.  

But the core concept looks good!

comments.author: playtetramental
comments.body:
Looks fun! Wishlisted.

Open to sharing more about your process?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Thanks what would you like to know?

replies.author: playtetramental
replies.body: I'd be interested to know the tools you use aside from Opus (Godot, Unreal, Blender) and a little about your method for the 3d environments and assets. The unique hand-drawn look really stands out.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: No tools outside of Opus and three.js. I just told it exactly what I wanted till I got the look right. That's really all you have to do.
